questions.question: With `city="New Delhi"`, what does `ls $city.txt` (unquoted) do?
options: Passes two arguments, New and Delhi.txt, because unquoted expansions are split on spaces
questions.explanation: Unquoted expansions undergo word splitting. Writing "$city.txt" keeps the value as one argument.

questions.question: A script is called as `./args.sh "New Delhi" Pune`. Which form passes exactly two arguments, New Delhi and Pune, on to another command?
questions.explanation: "$@" expands to each argument as a separate word, preserving spaces inside them. "$*" joins everything into one string, $* splits on spaces and $# is the count.

questions.question: For `f="report.final.csv"`, what does `${f##*.}` produce?
questions.explanation: ## removes the longest prefix matching *. which leaves only the extension. ${f%.*} would give report.final and ${f%%.*} would give report.

questions.question: Why can a script with `#!/bin/sh` that uses `[[ ]]` work on Fedora but fail on Ubuntu?
options: [[ ]] is only valid inside functions on Ubuntu
On Ubuntu /bin/sh is dash, which lacks Bash-only features, while on Fedora /bin/sh is Bash
questions.explanation: The shebang selects the interpreter. Ubuntu and Debian link /bin/sh to dash, a minimal POSIX shell, so Bash extensions fail there. Use #!/usr/bin/env bash for Bash scripts.
